production.note: US model years, from Kelley Blue Book (a database): the 2023 Huracán lists "Sterrato Coupe 2D" and the 2024 Huracán lists "Sterrato Coupe 2D" (kbb-huracan-2024), whose year selector ends at 2024. Carscoops (carscoops-sterrato, 30 November 2022): "Lamborghini will only only build 1,499 units starting in February 2023".

body.note: Raised two-door coupe (Carscoops calls it a "crossover" in the headline; it is the Huracán coupe body).

aspiration.note: Auto Bild: "5,2-Liter-V10-Sauger mit 610 PS und 560 Nm" (Sauger = naturally aspirated).

drivetrain.note: Quote: "It is combined with 7-speed dual-clutch transmission and electronically controlled all-wheel drive with rear mechanical self-locking differential."

transmission.note: "7-speed dual-clutch transmission" (Lamborghini LDF). No manual offered.

powerHp.note: Quote (Lamborghini model page): "Max. power (kW/CV) | 610 CV (449 kW) @ 8,000 rpm". 610 CV x 0.98632 = 602 hp. Carscoops (Chris Chilton): "602 hp (610 PS)". No separate US SAE rating was found, so powerStandard is DIN PS, as in the other Huracán records. Evo panel (evo-sterrato): "Power | 602bhp @ 8000rpm".

weightLb.note: DRY weight (step 4: a major magazine panel figure labelled dry). Quote (Evo spec panel, James Taylor, 18 December 2023): "Weight | 1470kg (dry)". 1,470 x 2.20462 = 3,241 lb. Corroborated by DriveArabia (drivearabia-sterrato, Gautam Sharma, 23 May 2023, spec box): "Weight 1,470 kg (dry weight)" and Carscoops (carscoops-sterrato, Chris Chilton): "the 3,241 lbs (1,470 kg) Sterrato". Auto Bild (autobild-sterrato) prints "1470 Kilo Leergewicht", the same figure under a kerb label, read as mislabelled. No Lamborghini or major-magazine curb weight (steps 1 to 3) was found; Lamborghini's model page gives no weight. No opened page says whether the dry figure assumes options. A car with fluids is heavier.
